newsitem.title: USA: Tatham completes first royalty relief bid.
newsitem.headline: Tatham completes first royalty relief bid.

text.p: Tatham Offshore Inc said Friday its application for deepwater royalty relief for the Sunday Silence field was deemed complete by the Minerals Management Service, effective November 13.
"We are pleased to have completed the first royalty relief application on record with the MMS," stated chief executive Thomas P. Tatham.

"The approval of Tatham Offshore's application for royalty relief is absolutely essential for the company to proceed with the timely development of the property," located in 1,500 feet of water offshore Louisiana on Ewing Bank blocks 958 and 1003.
Under the deepwater royalty relief legislation, the MMS is allowed up to 180 days to evaluate an application once the application is deemed complete, Tatham noted.

If approved by the MMS, royalty relief would provide for the abatement of the 12.5 percent federal royalty on at least the first 52.5 million equivalent barrels of oil produced from the Sunday Silence field.

Tatham Offshore noted it drilled the Ewing Bank 958 No. 1, the discovery well for the Sunday Silence field, in 1994. The Ewing Bank 1003 No. 1, a delineation well for the field, tested at a rate of some 8,700 barrels of oil and 5.4 million cubic feet of gas per day. Tatham Offshore owns a 100 percent working interest in the field.
